correctness.rationale: The Neumann kernel for -D d_xx+r with reset source r*mu yields the endpoint jump lambda/cosh(lambda L/2) times the odd hyperbolic-sine transform. Correcting by -J*sinh(lambda(x-L/2))/(Dlambda cosh(lambda L/2)) and imposing J=kappa*(p(L)-p(0)) gives the displayed positive current multiplier. Entire-function identity and density of odd polynomials identify exactly the reflection-antisymmetric signed measure. Jordan total-variation decomposition s>=|a| yields all valid probability laws mu=a+|a|+(1-m)sigma and uniqueness iff m=1. k+1 paired support sites give a nonzero signed kernel at k rates, perturbed into positive laws. Reflection and positive permeability give zero-current equivalence for interfacial entropy, and expansion at r downarrow0 gives mean source-position slope. Independent finite-atom check confirms Green jump and reflection invisibility.

value.rationale: Determining precisely what a one-dimensional physical boundary observable can and cannot recover, including the sharp nonlinear positivity restriction and the finite-vs-continuum observation boundary, is a meaningful inverse problem. The complete probability-law fibre and unit-variation uniqueness criterion are stronger than a forward flux formula, with a useful impossibility result for finite scanning.

limitations: Signed exact population currents on a rate set with positive accumulation, fixed reset law, known D/L/kappa and no atoms at interface. A finite number of rates or entropy-only data cannot identify general laws.
